1.why: verify-reset requires the token hash to match session.resetTokenHash and token.accountId/sessionId before accepting it.

2.why: Reset tokens are bound to sessionId and accountId, so the same code is rejected for any other session/user.

3.why: reset-password never deletes or invalidates other entries in the sessions map, so prior sessions keep working.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and HSTS, but the code does not explicitly pin a TLS version.

5.why: Reset tokens and emails are SHA-256 hashed and passwords bcrypt-hashed; appropriate protection though not reversible encryption.

6.why: No real email body includes private fields; responses use a generic message and only a simulation test token.

7.why: Emails/passwords are validated and length-limited; client renders only via textContent, not raw HTML.

8.why: Redirects use fixed CONFIGURED_HTTPS_ORIGIN after Host checks; no user-controlled redirect targets.

9.why: There are no email templates that interpolate user-supplied HTML or scripts.

10.why: API errors are generic, but testToken and testMfaCode are returned and written into the on-page log list.

11.why: Initial password bcrypt hash and the MFA secret '246810' are hardcoded in the source.

12.why: MFA is always set to the fixed default code 246810, so default credentials work.

13.why: VERIFY_FAILURE_LIMIT, mfaAttempts, and resetRequestTimes rate limits lock or reject further tries.

14.why: request-reset always returns the same generic message and a same-shaped token whether or not the email matches.

15.why: Tokens come from secureToken(32) (cryptographic random) and are stored/checked as user- and session-specific hashes.
